pos.personaBrief: Spain 2010-12 held 65-68% possession and faced the fewest shots (28), so the ball was a defensive tool; Del Bosque accepted opponents sitting deep and Spain still played patiently.

pro.personaBrief: Spain rarely played long and Arsenal built patiently, though Arteta's 2020-21 version loosened toward directness; safe, short circulation dominated.

est.personaBrief: Spain concentrated passing in small areas with a false nine, and Arteta's Arsenal split the pitch into zones and triangles, so structure plus close combinations.

lar.personaBrief: Spain crowded the centre (Cox) and Arsenal's absolute width was among the lowest in the league; width was only a late fix.

blo.personaBrief: Spain pressed high and won tackles high up, with a counterpress to keep the ball; they did drop 10-15m deeper when tired, and Arsenal used a compact mid-block with selective triggers.

mar.personaBrief: Defensive order and compactness with spatial responsibility (Arsenal zonal/man mix, zero corners conceded); no evidence of man-marking stars.

pla.personaBrief: Del Bosque said Spain would not change style and Spain never moved to a plan B; Arteta learned the system must fit the players, but the model stayed the base.

res.personaBrief: Possession as risk control to win: efficiency built on defensive order, pragmatic when needed (WSC), shutting games down with control rather than chasing spectacle.

sis.personaBrief: Collective control and defensive order for all, with first ten ever-present; Arteta stated the system must fit the players, yet roles stay defined.

jog.personaBrief: Technical players with ball security, two deep midfielders valued for passing; lacked height and counter speed, and physical duels were not the focus.

bas.personaBrief: Del Bosque used an ever-present experienced core; Arteta leaned on a young squad by necessity, but titles came first.

lid.personaBrief: Del Bosque was calm, cajoling the squad and unflappable; Arteta demanded respect and rules (follow or be out).
